concepts.def: Identifying a commercial opportunity and taking the financial risk of developing a new product or business to exploit it.
Gathering data about consumers through surveys, interviews and focus groups to identify needs, gaps in the market and likely demand.
Product development driven by consumer demand: designers respond to what the market asks for, such as healthier foods or smaller devices.
Product development driven by new technology or materials, where innovation creates products consumers did not know they wanted.
The identity of a product or company — name, logo, values and reputation — built to create recognition, trust and customer loyalty.
Raising finance for a new product from many small contributors through online platforms, often pre-selling the product before manufacture.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Enterprise & Marketing — a core area of A-Level Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Enterprise & Marketing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Enterprise & Marketing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What are the 4 Ps of the marketing mix?
options: Product, price, place, promotion
Plan, prototype, produce, profit
People, power, process, packaging
Purpose, patent, publicity, price
Product development driven by consumer demand
Products created because a new technology became available
Removing failed products from shops
Discounting products to clear stock
Raising finance from many small contributors via an online platform
A government grant for new factories
A bank loan secured against machinery
Selling shares on the stock exchange

mcqs.q: What is the main purpose of branding?
options: To build recognition, trust and customer loyalty
To reduce the cost of raw materials
To meet safety legislation
To speed up the assembly line

mcqs.q: What is the difference between market pull and technology push?
options: Market pull means consumer demand drives development of a product; technology push means a new technology or material inspires a product the market hasn't asked for yet.
Market pull means pulling unsuccessful products off the shelves.
Technology push is advertising gadgets on social media.
A brand is the barcode used at the checkout.

mcqs.q: Is a brand just a logo?
options: A brand is the barcode used at the checkout.
No — a brand is the whole identity: name, logo, design language, values and reputation, shaping what customers expect from every product the company makes.
A brand is only the logo printed on the product.
Technology push is advertising gadgets on social media.

mcqs.q: Does successful crowdfunding guarantee a product will reach the market?
options: A brand is the barcode used at the checkout.
No — crowdfunding provides finance and evidence of demand, but backers carry risk: funded projects can still fail in manufacture, certification or distribution.
Once a product is crowdfunded it is certain to be manufactured and delivered.
Crowdfunding is a government scheme that insures new products.
